headline_fact: Article 14 uses the words “any person,” rather than “any citizen.”
summary: One small wording difference helps explain who a constitutional provision concerns.
did_you_know: The wording of each provision matters.
core_mechanics: Article 14 addresses the State and refers to any person within the territory of India.
why_it_matters: Do not assume every constitutional protection uses the same description of the people it concerns.

in_depth_breakdown.real_world_application: Read the scope of a constitutional provision before drawing conclusions.

learning_takeaways: Read who the provision concerns before applying it.

share_text: Read the people, the public authority, and the limits named in a constitutional provision.

constitution_lesson.question: Does Article 14 refer only to citizens?
constitution_lesson.learning_goal: Identify who this provision concerns without assuming the same scope for every right.

opening_scenario.title: Consider a hypothetical public office
opening_scenario.situation: A visitor hears someone say that every constitutional protection is only for citizens. They open Article 14 to check the wording.
opening_scenario.question: What should they look for first?

big_idea.explanation: Start with the words that identify the people concerned. Article 14 refers to any person within the territory of India.

constitutional_basis.title: Equality before law
constitutional_basis.plain_meaning: The State must not deny equality before the law or equal protection of the laws to any person within the territory of India.
constitutional_basis.legal_effect: This is a fundamental-right provision directed at the State. Its wording does not restrict its protection to citizens.

explanation_steps.title: Identify who the provision addresses
explanation_steps.explanation: Article 14 addresses the State. That is the public authority named in this provision.

explanation_steps.title: Read who it concerns
explanation_steps.explanation: The text uses “any person.” Do not silently replace this with “any citizen.”

explanation_steps.title: Keep the stated scope
explanation_steps.explanation: The text refers to the territory of India. Read that condition with the protection it describes.

worked_example.title: Check the claim before accepting it
worked_example.situation: In the hypothetical office, the visitor reads Article 14 rather than relying on the broad claim.
reasoning_steps: Identify the people and public authority it names.
Keep the conclusion limited to that provision.
worked_example.outcome: The claim that Article 14 refers only to citizens does not match its wording.
worked_example.limits: This example does not decide a dispute or identify a legal remedy for any person.

who_it_concerns: Any person within the territory of India, as stated in Article 14.
limits: This lesson explains the wording of one provision, not every equality dispute.
Other constitutional provisions can use different language about who they concern.

common_confusions.confusion: Person and citizen mean the same thing here.
common_confusions.clarification: Read the actual word used by the provision. Article 14 uses person; this lesson does not replace it with citizen.

diagram.title: Read the authority and the people separately
diagram.caption: A schematic reading guide for Article 14, not a decision about a legal dispute.
diagram.description: The map connects the State addressed by the provision with the people described in its scope.
limitations: This map omits legal interpretation and remedies.

nodes.label: The State
nodes.detail: The authority addressed by the provision.

nodes.label: Any person
nodes.detail: Read with the territorial condition in the text.

edges.relationship: Read the protection together with its stated scope.

key_terms.definition: A particular part of a legal document.

knowledge_checks.question: Which word does Article 14 use: person or citizen?
knowledge_checks.explanation: Keep the wording of the relevant provision when explaining its scope.

knowledge_checks.question: Does this lesson establish the scope of every constitutional right?
knowledge_checks.explanation: It explains one provision. Other provisions need their own reading.

takeaways: Start with the wording of the relevant provision.
Identify the authority, people and conditions it names.
Keep an example’s conclusion within its limits.
